note: The proof spine of this manuscript is structural apart from three computations, all registered below: the characteristic polynomial and discriminant of Euler multiplication on the rank-four even cohomology of a minimal rational ruled surface, computed from the presented small quantum cohomology; the emptiness of the Eckardt scheme of explicit members of the nonstandard A_5-cubic pencil; and the elimination determining the Eckardt locus and the singular locus of that pencil as a whole, which is what separates it from the explicit coprime-degree family of Yang, Yu and Zhu.  Every other statement invokes no enumeration, certificate, or symbolic program as a premise.

hirzebruch-euler-spectrum.role: Computes the matrix of Euler multiplication on the rank-four even cohomology of a Hirzebruch surface in the two specialized Novikov values, together with its characteristic polynomial, the discriminant of that quartic, the factorization of the quartic on the degeneracy locus of the discriminant, and the dimension of the eigenspace at the repeated root.  It runs six independent cross-checks on the presentation: the classical cohomology ring at the origin; the Novikov grading; an elimination of the two divisor generators; a splitting or resultant computation of the discriminant; self-adjointness of Euler multiplication for the trace form; and the relations computed directly from the genus-zero invariants of the Hirzebruch surface of index two.  It does not establish that the presented ring is the small quantum cohomology of the surface; that reduction is argued in the manuscript.

a5-pencil-eckardt-locus.role: Determines the Eckardt locus and the singular locus of the whole nonstandard A_5-cubic pencil, rather than of individual members.  In the six-point model, with F_b the defining form in the chart a = 1, it saturates the ideal generated by F_b together with the hundred three-by-three minors of the Hessian of F_b by the irrelevant ideal, which is what makes the statement projective, and eliminates the five coordinates; the result is b(b^2+3b+9).  The same computation on the Jacobian ideal alone gives b(b+6)(b^2-3b-9)(7b^2+3b+9), whose zero set is the reduced locus of singular parameters, that is the radical of the pencil's discriminant and not the discriminant, which has degree eighty.  The single pencil point outside the chart, the cubic T_1, is treated separately and has empty singular locus and empty Eckardt scheme.  The elimination is a Groebner basis computation over Q, trusted as an execution of Singular; it does not produce a certificate.  Two independent cross-checks are tracked in this same bundle.  The first, a5-pencil-eckardt-locus-f32003.txt, repeats both eliminations over F_32003 and returns the identical Eckardt polynomial and the same factor shape for the singular locus.  The second, a5_pencil_eckardt_sweep.py and its output, recomputes both loci over F_11, F_19, F_29, F_31 and F_41 by direct enumeration of P^4(F_q), sharing no code with the elimination, agrees on both, and additionally finds thirty Eckardt points on each Eckardt member, matching the Fermat cubic threefold's own count computed by the same detector.  That count is what identifies the two Eckardt members as the Fermat members; the manuscript argues the identification, and this bundle supplies the count it rests on.
commands: nix shell nixpkgs#singular --command Singular -q verification/a5-pencil-eckardt-locus.sing > verification/a5-pencil-eckardt-locus.txt
uv run --with numpy python3 verification/a5_pencil_eckardt_sweep.py > verification/a5-pencil-eckardt-sweep.txt
uv run --with numpy python3 verification/a5_pencil_eckardt_sweep.py --check verification/a5-pencil-eckardt-sweep.txt

a5-pencil-eckardt.role: Two tracked outputs.  The first records the model checks: that the six-point action of A_5 on P^1(F_5) has the stated triple orbits, that the invariant cubics on the sum-zero subspace form a pencil, that the second generator T_1 is A_5-invariant and not S_6-invariant, and that the monomial model induced from a cubic character of a point stabilizer has two invariant directions, both fixed by all sixty group elements, one of them the Fermat form.  The second records, for explicit members of both models, the dimension of the affine cone cut out by the equation together with its Jacobian ideal, and the dimension and degree of the cone cut out by the equation together with the three-by-three minors of the Hessian: the first certifies smoothness, the second the emptiness or the degree of the Eckardt scheme.  Five members of the six-coordinate model and three of the monomial model are smooth with empty Eckardt scheme; the Fermat cubic threefold, which is a member of the pencil and appears explicitly in the monomial model, returns thirty Eckardt points as a control in both rings; and two members of the coprime-degree normal form of Yang, Yu and Zhu return nonempty Eckardt schemes.  It does not compute the finite exceptional set of the pencil, and it certifies nothing about singular members.
